name: highlight.js
description: The most widely deployed JS highlighter; auto-detection, zero-dependency, runs in browser and Node

host-language.comment: Implemented in JavaScript; the npm package also ships TypeScript type definitions, but the source and grammars are JS.

form-factor.comment: Library for browser (script tag/CDN/ESM) and Node (CommonJS/ESM). No first-party CLI.

license.comment: BSD 3-Clause; 'Copyright (c) 2006, Ivan Sagalaev'. Third-party grammars listed in SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES.md are separate packages with their own licences.

package.comment: npm package 'highlight.js'; prebuilt browser/CDN builds are published as '@highlightjs/cdn-assets'.

first-release.comment: Created by Ivan Sagalaev in 2006 (LICENSE copyright year). The GitHub repo dates from 2011 and the first npm publish from 2011-07-15.

latest-version.comment: npm dist-tag latest as of 2026-11-18. CHANGES.md on main already lists an unreleased 11.12.1.

engine-model.comment: Declarative mode trees of begin/end regexes interpreted by a JS state machine.

regex-engine.comment: Grammars compile to native JavaScript RegExp objects; no external regex engine.

embedded-languages.comment: Via the mode 'subLanguage' attribute: the xml/html grammar highlights <style> contents as css and <script> contents as javascript out of the box. subLanguage can also auto-detect among a set of languages.

language-auto-detection.comment: highlightAuto(code, languageSubset) runs all (or a subset of) grammars and picks the highest relevance score; returns secondBest as well. highlightElement auto-detects when no language class is present.

filename-extension-mapping.comment: No filename/shebang/mime lookup API. Grammars declare aliases (several of which happen to be extensions like 'js', 'py'), resolvable via getLanguage()/registerAliases, but there is no dedicated filename or path mapping.

resumable-line-state.comment: v10 accepted a 'continuation' argument to highlight(); v11 removed it from the public API ('only intended for internal library usage'), and the result's _top is now private.

incremental-reparsing.comment: Each highlight() call processes the full input; no edit-reuse mechanism.

semantic-distinctions.comment: Pure regex lexer. Grammars emit scopes like title.function or params from regex context, but there is no syntax tree or locals tracking.

bundled-languages.comment: v11.12.0, checked 2026-11-18: 193 core grammars in the full npm/Node build (the site says 193; the src/languages directory has 194 .js files). The default highlight.min.js CDN build includes only a smaller 'common' subset. SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES.md also lists ~114 third-party grammar packages that aren't bundled.

grammar-format.comment: Grammars are JS functions that return a mode-tree object.

grammar-ecosystem-compatibility.comment: Only consumes its own grammar format; no TextMate/Sublime/tree-sitter import.

runtime-grammar-loading.comment: registerLanguage(name, definition), unregisterLanguage and registerAliases are available at runtime (the docs describe them as mostly internal, but they are the documented way to add third-party grammars).

lazy-grammar-loading.comment: No built-in on-demand loader. The full build registers every grammar up front. To keep bundles small you import lib/core plus individual lib/languages/* modules yourself (statically or with your own dynamic import).

grammar-accuracy.comment: Hand-maintained regex grammars that don't track an upstream grammar. They are kept fairly current (11.12.0 added Python t-strings and Lua 5.5 keywords), but modern/nested syntax still has gaps, e.g. open issue #4550 (Sep 2026): TypeScript generic function declarations lose name/params highlighting. Rated 3 per the guideline.

bundled-themes.comment: Repo main, checked 2026-11-18: 90 stylesheets in src/styles plus 176 in src/styles/base16. highlightjs.org claims '516 themes', apparently counting differently (e.g. the minified variants listed on the demo page).

theme-format.comment: A theme is a plain CSS file that styles .hljs-* scope classes. The base16 collection is ported to the same CSS format, not loaded as base16 YAML.

token-classification.comment: Closed set of scopes (keyword, string, title.function, ...) rendered as hljs-* classes. Grammars may map custom names via classNameAliases.

css-class-output.comment: Class-only output with a configurable classPrefix (default 'hljs-'). There is no inline-style mode.

multi-theme-output.comment: Borderline. One class-based render works with any theme because themes ship as swappable stylesheets (e.g. github.css / github-dark.css, which can be switched with a media query). The Research Notes count this, but there is no built-in CSS-variable or dual-theme mechanism, and the theme guide doesn't document light/dark switching.

public-token-api.comment: highlight() returns only an HTML string ('value') plus metadata. The internal token tree is exposed as _emitter, which v11 marks private ('subject to change at any time'). The documented Emitter interface (addText/startScope/endScope) is an input hook for custom grammar parsers (__emitTokens), not a token output API.

ir-kinds.comment: No documented intermediate representation. Output is an HTML string (or in-place DOM mutation via highlightElement), and the token tree is private (_emitter). Wrappers like lowlight rebuild a hast tree from it, but that is outside this package.

serializable-ir.comment: There is no public IR to serialize.

theme-resolved-tokens.comment: Themes are CSS only, and the library never resolves colours.

source-offsets-in-ir.comment: There is no public IR, so no source offsets are exposed.

custom-formatter-api.comment: The plugin API (before/after:highlight, before/after:highlightElement) can rewrite input or post-process the result, but there is no documented way to replace the HTML emitter/renderer.

line-transforms-decorations.comment: No built-in line/range decoration mechanism. Plugins can only post-process the final HTML string or the element.

output-formats.comment: HTML with hljs-* classes only. Terminal output (cli-highlight), hast (lowlight) and the Vue component are community or separate projects.

line-numbers.comment: Deliberately unsupported ('not an oversight but a feature'); the docs point to third-party plugins.

streaming-output.comment: Highlights complete buffers only. The continuation argument that allowed chunked highlighting was removed from the public API in v11.

terminal-ready.comment: No ANSI output. Terminal use needs a third-party converter such as cli-highlight.

native-dependencies.comment: Pure JS with zero runtime dependencies.

runs-in-browser.comment: Script tag, CDN, ES modules/importmap, and Web Worker usage are all documented.

wasm-build.comment: Pure JS with no WASM build.

synchronous-api.comment: highlight() and highlightAuto() are synchronous, and no async initialisation is required.

bindings-ports.comment: scrivo/highlight.php is a community PHP port of highlight.js (~710 stars, 9.18.x stable line). There are no official bindings.

core-package-size.comment: Core engine only, no grammars: @highlightjs/cdn-assets@11.12.0 es/core.min.js is 20,501 B minified and ~8.2 KB gzipped (gzip -9, measured 2026-11-18). Bundlephobia reports the full npm package entry (all 193 grammars) at 299.9 kB min+gzip.

throughput-tier.comment: Contested. In the reproducible speed-highlight benchmark (Node 26, M4; hljs 11.11, HTML output), highlight.js is within 1.1x of Prism on 1 KB inputs and faster than every other comparison candidate on 16 KB and 128 KB inputs; only speed-highlight, which is not a candidate, is faster. The chsm.dev Jan 2025 benchmark (single TSX sample, method not described) has Prism ~2x faster, which would mean 'fast'.

initialization-cost.comment: Cold start (import plus first highlight) measured at 19 ms in the speed-highlight benchmark (Prism 8.6 ms, Shiki JS engine 169 ms). Loading only lib/core plus a few grammars is likely lighter, but that wasn't measured.

github-stars.comment: Snapshot 2026-11-18 (GitHub API stargazers_count; the repo page shows 25.0k).

monthly-downloads.comment: npm, 2026-10-18 to 2026-11-16. Inflated by heavy transitive use (e.g. via lowlight and cli-highlight).

last-release.comment: 11.12.0 was published to npm 2026-08-12 (11.11.2 the day before).

maintenance-status.comment: 11.12.0 was released Aug 2026 with grammar fixes and a new grammar and theme. As of 2026-11-18 there are commits on main through Nov 2026, with unreleased 11.12.1 changes.

documentation-quality.comment: Read the Docs site with API reference, language/mode guides, theme guide and plugin API, plus SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES.md, an interactive language/theme demo and version upgrade guides. Internals such as the emitter are intentionally undocumented.

notable-users.comment: highlightjs.org lists these under 'Trusted by'. Downstream wrappers like lowlight and cli-highlight are also built on it.

bus-factor.comment: Core team: Josh Goebel (maintainer) and Vladimir Jimenez. Former maintainers include the original author Ivan Sagalaev. Releases are published by joshgoebel, so in practice it relies largely on one person.
